newsitem.title: UK: Pearson hits new high on vague bid talk.
newsitem.headline: Pearson hits new high on vague bid talk.

text.p: Shares in Pearson hit another record high on Wednesday as rumours about a possible bid for the British media group refused to die, traders said.
This time the name of Carlton Communications was in the frame as a possible predator with talk it was lining up an 800p per share bid, valuing Pearson at 4.56 billion stg.
Carlton declined to comment on the rumours but analysts were sceptical despite the recent rise in the shares.
Pearson was up 6p at 762-1/2p in early trading after hitting a new high of 770p shortly after the open. The shares climbed 18-1/2p yesterday in a late flurry of buying interest.

"I don't believe it. There would be dilution if Carlton took them on. It's not Green's style to have a contested bid and shareholders would be likely to give the new Pearson mangement the benefit of the doubt in any hostile bid," said Henderson Crosthwaite analyst Lousie Barton.

Traders said a stock shortage was exacerbating the upward move in the stock with few sellers around given the possibility of either a bid or a shake-up of the group's operations after the naming of a new chief executive and chairman two weeks ago.
